# Noise audit: train vs test (generated by `python -m src.noise_audit`)

Raw names and addresses, up to 300,000 random records per (split, source, country). France has no training data, so France test is compared with the mean of train India and US for the same source. Shares are fractions of records. **Flagged** = test at least 1.5x train and at least 0.5 points higher.

## Reading the audit and how normalize.py (Pass 7) covers each noise type

- **S1 is clean in every split; the noise is in S2/S3.** For India and US, test S2/S3 noise matches train within a few percent, so test is not noisier than train there. **France is the difference**: accented Latin letters in 16-28% of France names and addresses (real accents such as 'Merignac' plus injected ones such as 'Comite' with a cedilla), which train never shows in addresses. This is consistent with Pass 5 gaining far more on the leaderboard (+0.066) than on eval (+0.013): eval has no France.
- Accents (France; also ~5-7% of India/US S2/S3 names): anyascii folding of every non-ASCII character.
- Indic scripts (India S2/S3: 18-28% of names, ~14% of addresses in Devanagari alone; also Bengali, Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam): transliteration with anyascii; transliterated legal forms (praivet/praibhet/piraivet/praivrr, limited/limitet/limirrd/limtid, 'pra li', elelpi) map to pvt / ltd / pvt ltd / llp.
- URL / domain names (3-4% of S2/S3 names), @ or # (~1%): protocol, www., TLD and leading @/# stripped.
- Trailing 6-12 digit numbers (~0.3%): stripped after a space, - , en dash or #.
- Bracketed text (6-10%): brackets become spaces, content kept (it is usually part of the name); empty brackets and [..] removed as junk.
- Doubled words (~2.3% of S2/S3 names): consecutive duplicates collapsed.
- Junk tokens (N/A, <NULL>, ##, --): removed from names and addresses (~4.5% of S2/S3 addresses).
- '#' before a number in addresses (5-11%): punctuation becomes a space, so '##19821' -> '19821'.
- Case (uppercase share differs by source): everything is lowercased.
- French legal forms and street words (EURL, SCI, SARL, SAS, SASU, SA, SNC, SCOP; rue/r, av, bd, pl, all, imp, ch, rte, fbg, sq): Tables 5.3 / 5.4 extended; 'r' -> 'rue' only for French addresses.
